title: Build the runner that reads the verb surface and performs the work
description:
The portal has the whole gated surface and nothing drives it. GET /api/agent/inbox returns new turns plus a cursor plus calls awaiting approval; POST /api/agent/message posts the agent's turn; POST /api/agent/verb requests one of the 24 verbs and answers 200 executed, 202 awaiting an operator, 400 unknown or missing arguments, 403 forbidden, 501 declared but unwired, 502 ran and failed. Missing piece: a process that polls the inbox from its cursor, hands the conversation and the verb vocabulary to omp, and turns what omp decides into verb calls - then reports the evidence the portal read back rather than its own account of it.

Shape that follows from decisions already taken. It holds no model credentials: omp owns authentication (omp auth-broker login, omp acp over stdio), so the runner starts omp rather than embedding a provider. It runs as its own OS user with no sudo, no read access to .env and no git credential for a parent remote, because upstream_push is forbidden by absence rather than refusal. It never shells out: the verb list is the entire vocabulary. A 202 is not a failure - it means an operator has to confirm, so the runner waits and keeps reading the inbox rather than retrying. An unanswered question blocks the action instead of resolving into a guess.

Acceptance: with the bridge enabled and omp authenticated, an operator types a request on /admin/agent and the runner answers there; a read verb executes and its evidence appears in the conversation; a mutating verb appears as a pending approval and only runs after the operator approves it; a forbidden verb is reported as refused without a retry loop. Nothing in the runner can widen what the portal allows.

title: Cover the admin site end to end, behind one command that runs everything
description: Measured 15 Aug: internal/app/server.go registers 89 routes, 49 under /admin, 33 of those POST forms - and 32 admin routes are named in no test at all. Existing coverage is 328 Go tests, 45 Python tests and 5 hostops scripts, with no single entry point: CI is the only place the whole set runs, which is how shellcheck stayed red on scripts/republish-profiles.sh for weeks unnoticed. Two halves. First, exercise every admin route the way an operator does - the action itself, the refusal without admin auth, the refusal with a missing or stale CSRF token, and the refusal for a malformed world or profile. Second, one command that runs every gate so a contributor sees the whole build without reading ci.yml. Why it matters here specifically: this project shipped a client installer that would not start, a setting inverted, and a per-second scene sweep, and each would have been caught by a test asking whether an operator action does what it claims.

title: Wire the seven verbs that need new host-agent operations
description: policy.yaml declares 24 verbs; internal/app/verbs.go executes 10 and refuses the rest with a reason. Seven refusals are only missing a host-agent operation, because the portal reaches the host solely through the agent socket: mod_check_updates, mod_notes, release_status, deploy_plan, mod_update, publish_profile, release_confirm. Each needs an operation in internal/agent/agent.go mapped to the hostops script that already does the work (tools/valheim_mods.py check-updates / notes / update / release-status / release-confirm, manage_mods.sh deploy for a plan-only diff, scripts/republish-profiles.sh for a publish). deploy_plan matters most: it is the confirmation prompt for deploy_apply, and without it an operator confirms a deploy without seeing the diff. publish_profile needs the evidence readback the policy demands - the setting value or a string unique to the new code, read out of the published artifact. repo_edit and plugin_build stay unwired by design (the agent works in its own checkout), world_restore keeps its typed operator confirmation, and the four forbidden verbs stay forbidden.
notes: Verified live on 14 Aug against a running portal: forbidden -> 403 refused, unwired -> 501 with the reason, mod_remove -> 202 pending, operator deny -> 303 and a system turn in the conversation, wired world_status -> 502 naming the missing agent socket. Audit rows and verb-call rows written for all four.
close_reason: Wired: mod_check_updates, mod_notes, release_status, deploy_plan, mod_update, publish_profile, release_confirm now execute through new host-agent operations, verified live against a running portal and agent

title: Keep growing the mod pack, in batches with play between them
description:
Grow the mod pack as far as it plays well. There is no target count: the operator dropped the
earlier "~300, typical servers run 300-500" framing, because what limits this pack is the frame
rate rather than the tooling. Every mod adds objects for the engine to cull and draw, and VR pays
that cost twice.

Working shape: add a batch, deploy, play a session, keep what earns its place. Tooling in place -
check-updates for what is newer, notes for the changelog of every version crossed, per-world
deploy as backup/stop/deploy/start, client-server parity enforced by the join handshake, and a
removal that records what it reached when it fails.
notes: Goal changed by the operator: no target count. The pack grows as far as it plays well rather than toward a number - earlier framing of ~300 mods (typical Thunderstore servers run 300-500) is dropped. What limits it is the frame rate, not the tooling: every mod adds objects for the engine to cull and draw, and VR pays that cost twice. So: add in batches, play a session, keep what earns its place.

title: Document the agent system, and make the README installable by a human or an agent
description:
README.md is 432 lines with an Installation section written for a person reading top to bottom, and it says nothing about the agent system: no policy.yaml, no verb surface, no /admin/agent, no bridge, no omp login, no beads workspace, and no mention of the three gates CI now runs.

Two audiences, one document, no second copy to drift. What a human needs: what this is, what it needs installed, the commands in order, and how to tell it worked. What an agent needs on top: no ambiguity about which directory it is in (three portal checkouts exist and only one is the dev checkout), every command copy-runnable with no placeholder left to guess, every environment variable named with what breaks when it is missing, an explicit statement of what it must never touch, and a way to verify each step rather than assume it. Write prerequisites as checkable commands, not prose. State required versions. Give the failure mode next to each step - what the error looks like and what it means - because an agent that cannot tell 'not configured' from 'wrong token' will invent a reason.

Cover, with the file that owns each: policy.yaml as the authoritative verb and approval definition; docs/agent-harness.md for how a harness consumes it; CLAUDE.md as the repository's law, and why AGENTS.md is not it here; the bridge endpoints and PORTAL_AGENT_BRIDGE_TOKEN_FILE, including that an absent token disables the bridge and answers 503 rather than 401; omp setup and omp auth-broker login, with the portal holding no model credentials; bd init --remote '' and why a bare bd init clones another project's tracker; and the three gates - check_agent_policy.py, check_perframe_work.py, check_beads_workspace.py - with what each refuses.

Keep the numbers honest and dated: 17 of 24 verbs execute today, 3 are refused by design, 4 are forbidden. When that changes, the docs change with it, and tools/check_agent_policy.py already fails CI when the verb table and the documentation disagree.

Acceptance: a fresh clone can be installed by following the README alone, by a person or an agent, with no step requiring knowledge that is not in the repository; and the agent sections match policy.yaml and internal/app/verbs.go, which the policy gate enforces.

title: Finish the operator chat interface on /admin/agent
description:
What exists: an admin-only page listing the conversation and every verb call with its class, status, approver, evidence and failure reason, Approve and Deny buttons on anything pending, a textarea to send a turn, and a warning when the bridge is disabled. It is a plain form-post page - static until reloaded, no auto-refresh, no streaming, no rendering of long evidence, no way to see a call's arguments in full, and the conversation is one unbounded list with a 100-turn cap on display.

To finish: refresh without a manual reload while a verb is running or awaiting approval; show a call's full arguments (a publish shows profile, client type and note; a release confirmation shows all four) so an operator approves what they can see rather than a summary; render evidence readably and collapse long output instead of one <pre> of everything; show a release diff against what is currently live beside a publish approval, which the policy names as the brake that replaces publish budgets; and make the page usable when the conversation is long. Keep it server-rendered and CSRF-guarded like the rest of the admin surface, and keep approval a deliberate two-button decision - never a keyboard default.

Acceptance: an operator can follow an in-flight request without reloading, sees every argument before approving anything player-facing, and can read the evidence without scrolling past a wall of text.

title: One command that runs every gate CI runs
description: A single entry point - scripts/check.sh, or a Makefile target - that runs: gofmt -l, go vet, go mod tidy verification, go build, go test -race, GOOS=windows go build, the Python suite, shellcheck scripts/*.sh, shellcheck -S style on hostops, the five hostops regression scripts, and check_agent_policy.py, check_perframe_work.py and check_beads_workspace.py. It must fail on the first broken gate and say which one. Reason: shellcheck was failing on scripts/republish-profiles.sh since at least 8f50113 and nobody noticed, because running everything meant reading ci.yml and copying eleven commands by hand.

title: Test every admin route: the action, and its three refusals
description: Walk the 49 /admin routes registered in internal/app/server.go. For each: it works for an authenticated operator; it is refused with 401 without admin auth; it is refused when the CSRF token is missing or stale; and it is refused for an invalid world or profile name. Reuse adminPost and adminPage from server_test.go rather than building a second harness. The 32 routes currently named in no test are the starting list, and these carry the most risk because they change worlds, releases or what players download: /admin/servers/{id}, /admin/releases/{id}/publish, /admin/releases/{id}/archive, /admin/mods/deploy, /admin/restores/{id}, /admin/access-apply, /admin/diagnostics/{id}, /admin/world-members/revoke.

title: scripts/republish-profiles.sh trips shellcheck SC2012
description: shellcheck -S style (what CI runs) reports SC2012 at scripts/republish-profiles.sh:79 - 'Use find instead of ls' - in deploy_pending(), which compares the staged plugin list against the deployed one to decide whether a deploy is outstanding. Present at 8f50113, 964df6c and fa1bbcb, so it predates the agent-surface work and means the shellcheck job has been failing on that file. Not fixed blind: 'ls -1 dir | sort -u' and 'find dir -maxdepth 1 -printf %f' differ on the directory entry itself and on dotfiles, and getting it wrong makes the portal either miss a pending deploy or claim one that is not needed. Fix it against a real deployed tree where the comparison can be observed both ways.
notes: Fixed with NUL-separated names rather than a straight ls->find swap. Measured: with newline-separated output, a directory named 'A<newline>B' renders identically to two named 'A' and 'B', so a genuine difference compares equal and a pending deploy is missed - ls misses it, find -printf '%f\n' also misses it, NUL-separated catches it. Verified against the real deployment: Hrafnheim/Vangard/Storgard/Doggerland all report nothing pending (matching the 0-differing-entries diff taken earlier), and a synthetic extra mod is still detected. shellcheck scripts/*.sh now exits clean, which it had not since at least 8f50113.
close_reason: Comparison is now NUL-delimited and unambiguous; CI's shellcheck command passes

title: Judge the 40 baselined per-frame scene searches
description: tools/perframe-baseline.txt lists 40 scene-wide searches reachable from Unity per-frame entry points, recorded when tools/check_perframe_work.py was introduced. Each needs one of: a real bound, a move off the frame path, or an annotation naming what stops it - then its baseline line goes. Start with AccessTools.TypeByName: this session measured a single TypeByName predicate at 100ms and a failed admin-id lookup at 1980ms, so the cost is established, not theoretical. Most sites early-return on a cached flag and are probably one-shot; CompanionVR.Tick (GameObject.Find), NeuralyzeVRFixes.DeactivateHotbars (FindObjectsOfType) and HudWatch.Resolve are the ones that looked genuinely repeated on inspection. Do not annotate a site without reading what actually bounds it - a stop condition that cannot be reached is exactly how the FastLink sweep shipped.
notes:
Baseline generated 14 Aug from tools/check_perframe_work.py --write-baseline; 40 sites across 12 files. CI fails on anything new.
Judged all 40. Root cause found by reading Harmony's own IL: AccessTools.TypeByName has no cache - Type.GetType(name), then AllTypes().FirstOrDefault over every type in every loaded assembly, then a SECOND full scan when that misses, then a log line. That is the 100ms measured for one predicate and the 1980ms for a failed admin lookup, and the failing case is exactly the one a null check cannot stop repeating. Fixed at the root: tools/vrfixes/TypeCache.cs caches by name INCLUDING misses, and all 94 call sites across 14 files now route through it. That removed 33 of the 40 sites. The remaining 7 were read individually and annotated with the mechanism that bounds each: HudWatch.Resolve and DumpHudTree set their one-shot flag before the scan; VRGuiBridge.Resolve short-circuits on _resolved; FastLinkTitle.Tick is bounded by the InWorld guard and MaxLooks; CompanionVR.Tick and DeactivateHotbars are called from the AdoptPollSeconds coroutine at 2 Hz rather than from a frame callback, and DeactivateHotbars shrinks to nothing because FindObjectsOfType returns only active objects. Baseline file deleted: CI now requires every scene search on a frame path to state its bound. Plugin rebuilt, 197632 bytes, TypeCache present in the binary.
Shipped 15 Aug: the type-lookup cache is live in all ten published profiles - hrafnheim-vr 2.5.91, the other three VR at 2.5.23, remainder at 2.2.x - each verified by finding TypeCache in the plugin inside the published artifact.
close_reason: All 40 judged: 33 removed by caching type lookups, 7 annotated with verified bounds, baseline retired

title: Vangard, Storgard and Doggerland have been down since 6 Aug
description: All three were stopped for mod work on 6 Aug (manage_mods.sh refuses to run against a live server) and never restarted; docker compose down removed their containers. Worlds are intact - last saves 6 Aug 03:41-03:42. 'Start' recreates the container via docker compose up -d; nothing is pending that blocks it.
notes: Evidence: Vangard.db 6 Aug 03:41, Storgard.db and Doggerland.db 6 Aug 03:42; no containers in docker ps -a; portal public_worlds shows them offline since 30 July.

title: Evaluate UseAmplifyOcclusion in a headset
description: Restored to VHVR's documented default (true) in hrafnheim-vr 2.5.90 after being disabled on 13 Aug while chasing frames that a per-second label sweep was actually costing. VHVR's own source marks it RECOMMENDED and its only condition - SSAO off in the game's graphics menu - already holds. Never yet looked at in a headset: confirm corners and contact shadows look right and the frame rate holds.
notes:
Evidence: hrafnheim-vr 2.5.90 profile artifact reads UseAmplifyOcclusion = true; VHVR source ValheimVRMod/Utilities/VHVRConfig.cs binds it default true, description begins RECOMMENDED.
Operator confirmed on 15 Aug: occlusion looks good in the headset. hrafnheim-vr ships UseAmplifyOcclusion = true, VHVR's documented default, and it stays.
close_reason: Operator evaluated it in a headset: looks good, stays at VHVR's default

title: Drive the admin site in a real browser once per release
description: The HTTP tests prove the handlers answer; they do not prove an operator can finish a task. Launch the portal, sign in as an operator and walk what matters: publish a profile, deploy mods to a world, approve an agent verb on /admin/agent, restore from a backup. Capture a screenshot of each. This is the class of check that would have caught a client installer which would not start despite passing every unit test it had.

title: Trim Hrafnheim server logging from Info level
description: config_merged/bepinex/BepInEx.cfg on Hrafnheim has console and disk logging at Info and WriteUnityLog=true. Costs the server's disk and CPU, not client frames. Changing it requires a server restart, so it is not free - batch it with other downtime.
notes: Read from Hrafnheim/config_merged/bepinex/BepInEx.cfg: two sections at 'Fatal, Error, Warning, Message, Info' plus WriteUnityLog = true.

title: Determine what AzuEPI 'Always Show All Slots' hides when off
description: The setting was measured as part of an 18.6ms per-open-frame inventory cost and left ON because nobody established which slots disappear when it is off. Read AzuExtendedPlayerInventory's source rather than guessing, then decide.
